267:     /** A verified implementation of a reader-writer lock,
268:     implemented using atomics and a reference count.
269: 
270:     When constructed, you can provide an invariant via the `Pred` parameter,
271:     specifying the allowed values that can go in the lock.
272: 
273:     Note that this specification does *not* verify the absence of dead-locks.
274: 
275:     ### Examples
276: 
277:     On construction of a lock, we can specify an invariant for the object that goes inside.
278:     One way to do this is by providing a `spec_fn`, which implements the [`RwLockPredicate`]
279:     trait.
280: 
281:     ```rust,ignore
282:     fn example1() {
283:         // We can create a lock with an invariant: `v == 5 || v == 13`.
284:         // Thus only 5 or 13 can be stored in the lock.
285:         let lock = RwLock::<u64, spec_fn(u64) -> bool>::new(5, Ghost(|v| v == 5 || v == 13));
286: 
287:         let (val, write_handle) = lock.acquire_write();
288:         assert(val == 5 || val == 13);
289:         write_handle.release_write(13);
290: 
291:         let read_handle1 = lock.acquire_read();
292:         let read_handle2 = lock.acquire_read();
293: 
294:         // We can take multiple read handles at the same time:
295: 
296:         let val1 = read_handle1.borrow();
297:         let val2 = read_handle2.borrow();
298: 
299:         // RwLock has a lemma that both read handles have the same value:
300: 
301:         proof { ReadHandle::lemma_readers_match(&read_handle1, &read_handle2); }
302:         assert(*val1 == *val2);
303: 
304:         read_handle1.release_read();
305:         read_handle2.release_read();
306:     }
307:     ```
308: 
309:     It's often easier to implement the [`RwLockPredicate`] trait yourself. This way you can
310:     have a configurable predicate without needing to work with higher-order functions.
311: 
312:     ```rust,ignore
313:     struct FixedParity {
314:         pub parity: int,
315:     }
316: 
317:     impl RwLockPredicate<u64> for FixedParity {
318:         open spec fn inv(self, v: u64) -> bool {
319:             v % 2 == self.parity
320:         }
321:     }
322: 
323:     fn example2() {
324:         // Create a lock that can only store even integers
325:         let lock_even = RwLock::<u64, FixedParity>::new(20, Ghost(FixedParity { parity: 0 }));
326: 
327:         // Create a lock that can only store odd integers
328:         let lock_odd = RwLock::<u64, FixedParity>::new(23, Ghost(FixedParity { parity: 1 }));
329: 
330:         let read_handle_even = lock_even.acquire_read();
331:         let val_even = *read_handle_even.borrow();
332:         assert(val_even % 2 == 0);
333: 
334:         let read_handle_odd = lock_odd.acquire_read();
335:         let val_odd = *read_handle_odd.borrow();
336:         assert(val_odd % 2 == 1);
337:     }
338:     ```
